One of the best games I've played in a long time - and for reasons I never thought I'd care a ton about.

The core gameplay and sandbox is very satisfying and rewarding.  Their long-tail progression systems are cool and give you plenty of reasons to continue to go on new mining assignments, and the customization offers some pretty interesting choices.  The soundtrack and audio design is top tier, the sheer amount of excitement and danger that happens when swarms come is 11/10.

But then they go the extra mile to really make you feel like an intergalactic space dwarf.
- The lobby is a fun-filled and surprisingly immersive place where you get to screw around while the world reacts to you appropriately (Management gets on the comms and tells you to stop dancing)
- The dwarfs all have absurd but fitting comments and personalities.
- There is just tons of flavor in places that you wouldn't think are important and yet they make all the difference.
- Tons and tons and tons of voice lines that really make the game world responsive to what's going on.
- The entire experience from lobby to level back to extraction and lobby is a single immersive experience.  Aside from a loading screen where it's required you get to experience it all rather than see a cut-scene/etc.  A minor detail but it takes a lot of work to do and makes the difference

None of this stuff is gameplay critical and yet it really takes the already excellent gameplay just the extra mile into a super engaging experience.

Rock and Stone!  Well done.

[h1][b]The Good[/b][/h1]
This game has character. It's everywhere, from the mission hub to the voice lines. Everything has this feeling of care put into that makes it the most charming games I've played. My friends and I still quote the game constantly, and one of our Discord server's favorite emotes is of the M.U.L.E.'s walk cycle. The gameplay captures what was fun about Left 4 Dead and Payday and layers on a rewarding weapon upgrading system, creating a loop of where you play a mission and then purchase the next upgrade for your gun/equipment. It's paced super well and doesn't feel grindy at all. The new overclocking system is neat, and I can't wait for the developers to get weird with them.

[h1][b]The Bad[/b][/h1]
Like all of these games of this type, sometimes you are going to have moments where you get screwed by RNG, but usually the chaos that creates is pretty fun. The only time I felt the grind setting in was when I had to promote characters. Getting all the weapons to unlock was well paced but the leveling up seemed to slow down drastically after getting the second weapon for that class.

[h1][b]Early Access[/b][/h1]
GSG has done a great job with handling the quirks of an EA game. They churn updates out at a slower rate than others but their updates are usually pretty large and fairly polished. Hotfixes are fast, and the developers are very communicative with the community.

[h1][b]TLDR[/b][/h1]
4/5, Great fun and very charming, but can get a little grindy as you approach the endgame.
